notes: Written from the maker's own source at commit 3a9441f, "v 2.3.4 buxfix mpe volume", which is the commit whose plugin.json carries the installed 2.3.4 and is also the head of the repository, together with manuals/README.md in the same tree and a render of every panel. No module in this plugin has a plugin-wide menu; BaseModuleWidget::appendContextMenu adds only a separator and then each module's own items. Every trigger input in the plugin goes through rescaleInput in src/util/Switches.cpp, which is rescale(v, 0.1, 2, 0, 1), so a Schmitt trigger that counts high above 2V and low below 0.1V. Five controls across the plugin were proved dead by reading every use of their parameter and are given lines saying so: the Tape Recorder's Motor Power screw, and the Tape Recorder Mixer's Tape Ducking knob, Ducking input, Erase input, Solo switch and Delay in samples screw. Tracker and MIDI Controller are both unfinished, and More Fun with Frames is a line-for-line copy of Fun with Frames.

lines: An emulation of a microcassette recorder: it writes whatever arrives at the audio input onto a tape kept inside the patch, and plays it back forwards or backwards at any speed
Halts the tape while a play button stays on, so the reels can be turned by hand
Runs the tape forward
Runs the tape backwards
Winds the tape forward at the multiple of play speed set by the Fast Speed screw; Ctrl and a click jumps to the next loop point instead, and Ctrl with Shift jumps to the end of the tape
Winds the tape backwards at the multiple of play speed set by the Fast Speed screw; Ctrl and a click jumps to the previous loop point instead, and Ctrl with Shift jumps to the start
Sets how fast the two winding buttons move the tape, from a quarter of play speed to 20 times it
Nothing in the module reads this screw. It sets the rise rate of a slew limiter on the tape speed whose every use is commented out of the source, so turning it changes no sound.
Sets the tempo the tape is measured in, 1 to 360 BPM; the tempo output pulses at it and the loop points are counted in its bars
Sets how many beats make a bar, 1 to 48, which fixes how much tape one bar covers
Sets the bar the loop starts at, 0 to 99
Sets the bar the loop ends at, 0 to 99

Turn a reel to move the tape by hand, which scratches the recording while a play button and pause are both on. Dragging near the rim brakes the tape and dragging at the centre leaves it at full speed.
Sets the loop start to the bar the tape has reached, and springs back off
Sets the loop end to the bar the tape has reached, and springs back off
The audio written to the tape, one polyphonic channel per track. It is also the bus back from the Tape Recorder Mixer, whose channels 5 to 8 erase a track and whose channels 9 to 12 saturate it.
Moves the loop start, one bar per 1/12V, added to the loop start knob and never taken below bar 0
Moves the loop end, one bar per 1/12V, added to the loop end knob and never taken below bar 0
Multiplies the tape speed by two to the power of the voltage, so 1V plays the tape an octave higher and -1V an octave lower
A rising edge toggles the pause button
The tape playback, one polyphonic channel per track, at ten times the value stored on the tape; while the tape is not running this carries the audio input instead
The speed the tape is running at as a pitch, one volt per octave; the sign is dropped, so a reversed tape reads at the speed a forward one would
5V for each beat and 10V for the first beat of a bar, one millisecond long, as the tape passes them; nothing comes out unless a play button is on
5V while the tape plays forward, -5V while it plays backwards, 0V when it is stopped
Note — recording is always on. Whenever a play button is on, whatever is at the audio input is written to the tape as it passes; to play a tape back without spoiling it, unpatch the audio input.
Note — the loop is off while the loop start and loop end read the same bar.
Note — the two winding buttons are momentary while a play button is on, and latch when the tape is stopped.
Note — the Ctrl in the winding shortcuts is Cmd on a Mac, and holding Ctrl or Ctrl and Shift while turning a reel moves the tape more slowly.
Note — the tape is kept inside the patch. Saving the patch writes the recording beside it as tape.wav, and saving a module preset writes a .wav of the same name beside the preset.
Menu — the text field at the top — holds the name written on the cassette label
Menu — Cassette Label: 1970, Red, Green, Purple, Brown, Rainbow, Stars, Snowflake, Flowers, Tape, Chip, Zzz — chooses the artwork printed on the cassette
Menu — Tape Length — sets how long the tape is, from MC 1 for one minute to MC 120 for two hours, and returns the transport to the start; MC 120 is barred while the track count is 4 Tracks
Menu — Track Count: Mono, Stereo, 4 Tracks — sets how many tracks the tape carries and how many channels the audio output has; 4 Tracks is barred on an MC 120 tape
Menu — Loop Mode: Cycle, Ping-Pong — chooses what happens at a loop point, Cycle jumping to the other end and Ping-Pong reversing the play direction; a new module comes up on Ping-Pong
Menu — Erase Tape — writes silence over the whole tape

TapeRecorder.notes: Read from the maker's source at commit 3a9441f, whose plugin.json carries the installed 2.3.4, and from manuals/README.md in the same tree. Motor Power is proved dead: it is passed to speedSlewLimiter.setRiseFall in two places, and every speedSlewLimiter.process call in TapeRecorder.cpp is commented out. The Loop Mode parameter has no widget of its own and is reached only through the menu. TapeRecorderMixer.notes: Read from the maker's source at commit 3a9441f, whose plugin.json carries the installed 2.3.4. Three controls and two jacks were proved dead by reading every use of their parameter: Tape Ducking, its CV input, the Erase CV input, the Solo switch and the Delay in samples screw are each referenced only where they are configured and where their widget is created. The plugin.json tags this module as a voltage-controlled amplifier and the panel prints duck, so the missing ducking is a real conflict with what the maker documents. A Link To Left Module parameter also exists and its widget is hidden at construction and never shown, so no click can reach it and it gets no line. The Erase knob is named Tape Erase Amount by the maker and what it actually does is set the level of the tape return mixed into the channel; the erasing itself is done by the record switch, which sends -10V down the bus.

FlyingFader.notes: Read from the maker's source at commit 3a9441f and manuals/README.md. PLUS_6_DB is 1.41253757 in src/util/Knobs.hpp, and the audio gain is the square of the fader value, which is why the parameter displays as 40 times the base-ten logarithm of its position. The MindMeld law is pow(value * 22.3606765, 1 / 1.5). When the CV input goes from unpatched to patched the module divides the fader value it had by the incoming voltage over ten and keeps that as the reference, which is what makes 10V hold the fader still. Four of this module's five parameters are internal state with no widget and cannot be clicked.

EqualDivision.notes: Read from the maker's source at commit 3a9441f and manuals/README.md. The output is simply the input multiplied by the interval in semitones divided by the number of steps and by the fine-tune factor, so twelve steps of an octave passes pitch through unchanged. Fine tune runs 0.97 to 1.03 and is shown as a percentage with 100 subtracted. The interval switch has fourteen positions and a new module starts on position 9, two octaves, with 33 steps. The display is drawn by the module and carries no controls.

CVFreqShift.notes: Read from the maker's source at commit 3a9441f and manuals/README.md. The shift is held as a multiple of the frequency of C4: the knob runs -10 to 10 and is multiplied by two to the power of the range switch divided by dsp::FREQ_C4, and the range switch's nine positions are powers of two from 1 to 256 times ten hertz. The modulation input is added in those same units without passing through the range switch, so one volt at the top of the modulation knob is one whole C4, 261.63Hz. The result is clamped at a frequency ratio of 0.0009766, which is ten octaves below C4, so the output never falls below -10V. The maker's manual leaves the Root Octave, Frequency Shift and Frequency Modulation sections empty and mentions a root octave control that is not on the module.

lines: A chord builder for Regen Modular Frames: it rescales four of that module's parameter outputs into semitone intervals and stacks them into a polyphonic chord above one incoming pitch
Sets how many notes the chord has, 2 to 5. The first note is the pitch at the note input, and each further note takes its interval from the next time-table input in turn.
Chooses how the voltage beside it is converted: both settings multiply it by 2.125, then linear subtracts 5V while linear with jump point subtracts 21.33V from anything above 10.625V
One of the four values to convert, taken from a parameter output of Frames, 0 to 10V
The root of the chord, one volt per octave
The gate for the chord, copied out on one channel per note
Patching anything here turns the chord into an arpeggio: each rising edge steps to the next note, the pitch and gate outputs drop to one channel, and a gate of 0V restarts from the root
The converted voltage from the input beside it
The chord, one polyphonic channel per note, root first; while a clock is patched it is the arpeggio on a single channel instead
The gate input on one channel per note of the chord, with 0V on the channel of any note whose time-table input reads 0V; while a clock is patched it is the gate input on a single channel instead
Note — a time-table input reading exactly 0V does not add a note: that voice holds the pitch it last had and its channel of the gate output is taken to 0V.
Note — the multiplier of 2.125 turns a full 0 to 10V sweep into 21.25V, one semitone for each step of a 256-step source, and the jump point folds the top half of that sweep to negative semitones.
Note — each converted output is only written while it is patched, and the chord and gate outputs only while they are patched.

Metronome.notes: Read from the maker's source at commit 3a9441f. The 39 tempo marks are a literal array in Metronome.cpp. The one-step-slower input has an off-by-one: the code reads if (--bpmIndex <= 0) bpmIndex = 38, so stepping down from the second mark, 42, lands on 208 rather than on 40, and 40 can never be reached from that jack. Stepping by two or three uses a subtraction loop and wraps correctly at the top. The timer only runs inside a test on the output being connected and the start button being on, so an unpatched metronome counts nothing. The tempo display and the numbers printed round the dial are drawn by the module and are not controls. The start button is a large round switch at the centre of the tempo knob; both can be clicked, the switch answering at the middle and the knob around it.

lines: A bank of sixteen tuned voices from one pitch: each takes the incoming pitch, multiplies its frequency by one whole number and divides it by another, and hands back its own pitch and velocity
Scales the velocity modulation input that feeds every channel at once, 0 to 100%
Scales the velocity modulation input beside it for this channel alone, 0 to 100%
Scales the velocity reaching this channel, 0 to 100%
Scales the pitch modulation input that feeds every channel at once; the setting is raised to the fourth power and it inverts below the middle
Scales the pitch modulation input beside it for this channel alone; the setting is raised to the fourth power and it inverts below the middle
Sets the whole number this channel's frequency is multiplied by, 1 to 96; it is the left half of the ratio on the display
Sets the whole number this channel's frequency is divided by, 1 to 96; it is the right half of the ratio on the display
Detunes this channel, adding up to 0.03V either way, which is 36 cents up or down
Switches this channel in and out. Only channel 1 is on when the module is added, and a channel that is off takes no place on the polyphonic outputs.
Restricts the module to its own group of four channels and clears whichever group was chosen before; with none of the four on, all sixteen channels are used
The gate for the voices, passed through to one channel of the gate output for each active channel
A retrigger for the voices, passed through to one channel of the retrigger output for each active channel
The velocity all the channels start from, before each channel's own velocity knob
Modulates the velocity of every channel, scaled by the knob beside it
Modulates the velocity of this channel alone, scaled by the knob beside it
The pitch all the channels are built on, one volt per octave
Modulates the pitch of every channel, scaled by the knob beside it
Modulates the pitch of this channel alone, scaled by the knob beside it
A rising edge chooses the mixture of the same number and clears the other three
The gate input on one polyphonic channel per active channel
The retrigger input on one polyphonic channel per active channel
Every active channel's velocity on its own polyphonic channel
This channel's velocity on its own, monophonic
Every active channel's pitch on its own polyphonic channel, one volt per octave
This channel's pitch on its own, monophonic, one volt per octave
Note — fifteen of the sixteen channels come up switched off, so a new module gives one voice at the pitch it is fed. Switch the further channels on before expecting a chord.
Note — the polyphonic outputs pack the active channels in order with no gaps, so channel 5 lands on polyphonic channel 2 if it is the second one switched on.
Note — the ratio of the two whole numbers is what the channel plays: 3 over 2 is a fifth above, 1 over 3 is two octaves and a fifth below, and 1 over 1 is the pitch as it came in.
Note — the module has no menu of its own beyond Rack's.

Harmonizer.notes: Read from the maker's source at commit 3a9441f. The harmonic and subharmonic knobs index an array of the base-two logarithms of 1 to 96, added and subtracted in the exponent, which is what makes the two numbers a frequency ratio. The fine knob runs 0.97 to 1.03 and its value minus one is added as volts, so its range is 0.03V, 36 cents, despite the maker displaying it as a percentage. A mixture takes the channels from four times its number minus four up to four times its number. The maker's manual describes this module as a rebuild of a vintage metronome, which is a copy-paste mistake in the manual. The panel prints Mixture and the maker's tooltips say Mixtur. The gate and retrigger outputs are written whether or not they are patched, and the sixteen per-channel outputs only while they are.

MIDIController.notes: Read from the maker's source at commit 3a9441f. The Test input is proved dead: the word inputs does not appear in MIDIController.cpp outside the enum and configInput. The knob named Test Parameter is written from every incoming controller but is only read back for controller 10. The voltage moves by the Adjust Movement knob times 250 divided by the number of frames since the last message for that controller, so the faster the encoder is turned the further it goes. After 5000 frames with no message the module sends the controller's value back out as a control change of the voltage times 12.7. The module has no entry in the maker's manual.

lines: Turns MPE from a MIDI keyboard into polyphonic control voltages, one polyphonic channel for each MIDI channel, with its own envelope shaping the pressure
Sets the first MIDI channel read, 1 to 16
Sets how many MIDI channels are read, and so how many channels every output carries; the count is trimmed so it never runs past MIDI channel 16
Bends the note-on velocity curve, from one raised in its middle at the left to one hollowed in its middle at the right
Pulls pitch bend towards whole semitones: at the left the bend passes through untouched, and turning it right narrows the band between semitones until the bend snaps from one to the next
Sets how slowly the volume falls away after a note held for less than about an eighth of a second; the higher the setting the longer the tail
Sets how slowly the volume falls away after a note held for more than about a fifth of a second; the higher the setting the longer the tail
Lengthens the fall after a short note in proportion to the modulation value, so a note played further up the key holds on longer
10V while a note is held on that MIDI channel, on one polyphonic channel per MIDI channel; with Gate Velocity Mode on it carries the note-on velocity instead
The pressure of the note through the envelope, taken from channel aftertouch, polyphonic aftertouch or control change 11, raised to the power of 1.3 and halved
The note's pitch with the pitch bend added, one volt per octave, with 0V for MIDI note 60
Control change 1 or 74 on that MIDI channel, 0 to 10V, smoothed
The note's pitch without any pitch bend, one volt per octave, with 0V for MIDI note 60
The pitch bend on its own, one volt per octave; a full bend is 4V, which is 48 semitones

Menu — Gate Velocity Mode — puts the shaped note-on velocity on the gate output in place of a flat 10V
Menu — Preserve Pitch after Note-Off — keeps the pitch bend applied once the note has ended, instead of dropping the pitch output back to the plain note
Menu — Panic — clears every note, gate, bend and modulation and re-opens the MIDI port

MIDIPolyExpression.notes: Read from the maker's source at commit 3a9441f and manuals/README.md. The module has no inputs at all; everything arrives over MIDI. Pitch bend is scaled as 4 times the 14-bit value minus 8192 over 8191, so a full bend is 4V or 48 semitones, the MPE default. Note pitch is the MIDI note number minus 60 over 12. The two menu-only settings, Gate Velocity Mode and Preserve Pitch after Note-Off, are parameters with no widget and cannot be clicked. The envelope switches between three laws on note-off by the note's length: under 0.125 seconds it uses the decay screw, over 0.1875 seconds the release screw, and between them a blend of the two.

lines: Merges pairs of polyphonic notes into one voice and slides between them: as the volume moves from one note to the other, the pitch and the modulation follow it across
Sets one end of the range of notes that may glide. With the lowest-note knob at or above the highest-note knob the range inverts, the red lamp lights, and the notes between them are left out.
Sets one end of the range of intervals that may glide, 1 to 127 semitones. With the minimum at or above the maximum the range inverts, the red lamp lights, and the intervals between are left out.
The pitches of the notes, one volt per octave, one polyphonic channel per note
How loud each note is, one polyphonic channel per note; the balance between two notes' volumes is how far their glide has travelled, and this jack sets the channel count of all three outputs
A modulation value for each note, one polyphonic channel per note, carried across the glide in step with the pitch
While a cable is here, a new note only joins a glide if the voltage is above 0V; with nothing patched every new note may join one
The pitch of each merged voice, one volt per octave, moving between the two notes in proportion to their volumes
The volume of each merged voice, the two notes added together
The modulation of each merged voice, moving between the two notes in proportion to their volumes
Note — nothing comes out until the volume input is patched, together with either the pitch input and pitch output or the modulation input and modulation output.
Note — with less than that patched, the module clears its note mapping and sets every output to no channels.
Note — a glide starts when a second note arrives over a sounding one, both notes fall inside the note range, and the interval between them falls inside the interval range.
Note — the two notes then share one output channel until the first of them is released.
Note — the two red lamps light to say their range has been turned inside out; they are not controls and cannot be clicked.
Note — the module has no menu of its own beyond Rack's.

XGlide.notes: Read from the maker's source at commit 3a9441f and manuals/README.md. The note knobs are snapped MIDI note numbers 0 to 127 displayed as note names C0 to G10, and the interval knobs are 1 to 127 semitones. Both ranges are compared in volts with a half-step of slack added at each end. How far a glide has travelled is the second note's volume over the sum of the two volumes, so it is the player's own pressure that moves it, not a clock. The manual is written for a LinnStrument and describes the left and right knob of each pair; the code treats the pair symmetrically and only cares which is the larger.

lines: Receives MIDI carried inside an audio signal, so a plugin hosted in VCV Host can send MIDI back into Rack; it decodes eight such streams and offers them to the rest of Rack as MIDI devices
Trims the level of the jack beside it until the lamp reads green, which is where the decoded bytes land exactly; the range is narrow because the level has to be right to the sample
The audio from a MIDI over Audio plugin, one sample per MIDI byte, with a negative sample ending each message
Note — adding this module registers a MIDI driver called MIDI over Audio, carrying eight devices named Port 1 to Port 8.
Note — to use what arrives at a jack, open any MIDI module in Rack, choose the MIDI over Audio driver, and choose the port of the same number as the jack.
Note — the lamp beside each jack reads the level: green is exact, yellow and orange are close, blue means the signal is too quiet and red that it is too loud.
Note — the lamps are drawn by the module and are not controls; they cannot be clicked.
Note — only three-byte MIDI messages are passed on; the decoder has a fixed three-byte buffer.
Menu — Panic — sends a note-off for all 128 notes on all 16 MIDI channels of all eight ports

MIDIOverAudio.notes: Read from the maker's source at commit 3a9441f and manuals/README.md. The driver is registered by the module's constructor, so it appears as soon as one of these is in the patch. MIDIOverAudioDriver::getInputDeviceName returns Port plus the device number. The lamp thresholds are isNear against -255.56 with tolerances of 0.44, 1.5 and 3 in src/modules/MIDIOverAudio/MIDIOverAudio.cpp. MIDI_MESSAGE_DATA_MAX_LENGTH is 3 in src/util/Drivers.hpp and the source carries a TODO about messages of other lengths. The trim knobs are excluded from randomisation.

CopyPastePreset.notes: Read from the maker's source at commit 3a9441f and manuals/README.md. The copying is done in CopyPastePresetWidget::step, which waits a few frames after the button goes down, copies the left neighbour's preset to the clipboard, then walks right pasting while consecutive modules share a model. The pulse is a dsp::PulseGenerator triggered with its default length of one millisecond.
